Mrs. Fisher: So you caught a big black sea bass, huh. That’s a good reason to celebrate. Good job kid.
You: Thanks.
Mrs. Fisher: It’s a good recreational fish, it’s common and puts up a good fight. Taste ain’t bad either. 
Mrs. Fisher: Here’s the thing. Although it has a bass in its name, black sea bass isn’t a sunfish like largemouth or smallmouth bass.
You: What? Really? 
Mrs. Fisher: Sunfishes live in freshwater. Do not confuse them with ocean sunfishes from the molidae family, that's a completely different class of fish.
You: What. I’m confused.
Mrs. Fisher: To put it shortly. Every freshwater bass is a sunfish, almost every saltwater bass is a serranidae and ocean sunfish are not sunfish. 
You: I feel like there’s a lot to unpack here…
Mrs. Fisher: Not every bass is a true bass and not every sunfish is a true sunfish. You will get a handle on it with experience.
You: Why is it so confusing? 
Mrs. Fisher: No idea to be honest, although I heard that some Lee Lantz guy in the 70s renamed patagonian toothfish to chilean sea bass so it would sell better.
You: What? Some guy could just rename a fish so it would sell better? That’s just stupid!
Mrs. Fisher: If it makes you feel better, the FDA accepted the name change. 
You: No, it doesn’t make me feel better! I feel like some shady deal took place…
